Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 529 Aerial Moose Survey - 2017 
 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit 529 (WMU 529) covers an area of 4,413 km 2, with 1,614 km2 comprising caribou range 
and 374 km2 designated as a Key Wildlife and Biodiversity Zone. The WMU is delineated in the north by 
Clearwater River and Whitemud Falls Wildland Provincial Park, in the west by Christina River, a tributary and the 
Canadian National Railways (CNR) railroad, in the east by the Saskatchewan border, and in the south by Winifred 
River.  
The area comprises mostly northern boreal mixedwood forest with several large waterbodies (Gordon, Gypsy, 
Birch, Garson, North Watchusk and South Watchusk lakes). The Bohn caribou range is found in the southern half 
of the WMU. The Gypsy Lake Wildland Provincial Park is found in the central north end of the WMU boundary.  
One First Nations reserve (Clearwater No. 175) is within the WMU, and two are directly south (Janvier No. 194 
and Cowpar No. 194A). 
A survey for moose was last conducted in 2009 using the random stratified block methodology. The moose 
population was estimated to be 157 individuals with a density of 0.04 moose/km 2. A total of 97 moose were 
classified and the bull:cow:calf ratio was estimated to be 60:100:87. See Table 1 for previous moose survey 
estimates for WMU 529 and surrounding WMUs. 
Hunting regulations currently split hunting for antlered moose into an Archery Only Season (August 25 to 31) and 
General Season (September 1 to November 30). 
The objective of the 2017 survey was to assess the status of the moose population in WMU 529 by determining a 
population estimate for moose based on density estimates and the age-sex composition. 
 
Survey method 
An aerial survey for moose was conducted from January 24 to 26, 2017, using distance sampling techniques 
(Buckland et al., 2001). A total of 230 north-south transect lines (survey effort = 2,101,658 km) were flown. Moose 
were classified by age class (adult or calf) and sex. All other wildlife sightings were recorded.  
Results 
A total of 114 moose were observed in 64 groups. The encounter rate was 0.03 moose/km 2 (90% confidence 
interval (CI) of 0.025 – 0.038). The estimated density was 0.089 moose/km 2 (CV 0.17, 90% CI 0.068 - 0.117) and 
the estimated population was 393 individuals (90% CI 298 – 517), with a coefficient of variation of 16.8 (Table 2). 
A total of 114 moose were successfully classified and the bull:cow:calf ratio was estimated to be 42:100:58.
